_comment: GPIO reference for the ESP32 family. Loaded by the CONTROL template's
binding block, which names this file in `variants_from`.
SOURCE: Espressif's own ESP-IDF 'GPIO & RTC GPIO' page per target, plus the
ESP32-P4 hardware design guidelines for that chip's UART0. Retrieved
2026-09-05. Where Espressif does not publish a number, this file says so
SCOPE: this describes what a pin can be asked to DRIVE, because that is what
the actuator map needs. ADC, touch and DAC capability are deliberately NOT
here: they do not affect whether a relay channel works, and half-checked
analog data in a file that looks authoritative is worse than no data.
Each group's `level` is what the validator does with it:
error  the pin cannot drive a relay here, or driving it breaks the board
warn   it will probably work, but something else wants the pin
(none) shown in the reference table, never flagged
A pin can be in several groups; the table shows all of them, and validation
reports each one that carries a level.

esp32.label: ESP32
esp32.subtitle: The original dual-core Xtensa — WROOM-32, WROVER, D0WD
esp32.absent_note: GPIO20, GPIO24 and GPIO28-31 are not bonded out.

groups.label: Input only
groups.note: GPIO{addr} is input-only on the ESP32: no output driver and no software pull-up or pull-down. A relay wired here can never be switched.

groups.label: SPI flash
groups.note: GPIO{addr} is wired to the module's SPI flash. Driving it crashes the board.

groups.label: PSRAM
groups.note: GPIO{addr} carries PSRAM on WROVER modules. Free on a plain WROOM, taken on anything with PSRAM.

groups.label: Strapping
groups.note: GPIO{addr} is a strapping pin. A relay holding it at reset can stop the board booting — GPIO12 in particular selects flash voltage and can brick a 3.3V module if pulled high.

groups.label: UART0 TX
groups.note: GPIO{addr} is UART0 TX — the console and the flashing line. Using it means no serial log and a harder reflash.

groups.label: UART0 RX
groups.note: GPIO{addr} is UART0 RX — the console and the flashing line. Using it means no serial log and a harder reflash.

groups.label: USB

esp32p4.label: ESP32-P4
esp32p4.subtitle: Dual-core RISC-V application processor — no radio at all
esp32p4.flash_note: The P4's flash sits on dedicated FLASH_* package pins, not on GPIOs, and its PSRAM is in-package and not pinned out — so unlike every other chip here, no GPIO is lost to memory. Espressif does not publish GPIO numbers for those signals because there are none.

groups.label: Strapping
groups.note: GPIO{addr} is a strapping pin. A relay holding it at reset can stop the board booting.

groups.label: USB-JTAG
groups.note: GPIO{addr} is the USB-JTAG pair. Using it costs you the USB serial console.

groups.label: UART0 TX
groups.note: GPIO{addr} is UART0 TX — the console and the download line — and a strapping pin as well.

groups.label: UART0 RX
groups.note: GPIO{addr} is UART0 RX — the console and the download line — and a strapping pin as well.

_esptool_map._comment: What `esptool chip_id` prints, lowercased and stripped, mapped to a variant above. flash-device.sh reads the chip off the silicon at step 3 and re-checks the map against it.
